A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same parameter-weighting attribution work. Both versions' main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix C report original classification, language-modeling and diffusion experiments, including LDS, mislabeled-data detection, tail-patch and semantic-attribution results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds noise-robustness experiments, another loss ablation, a representation-distance comparison and Llama3-8B-Instruct results.

M1.justification: The proposed query-side weighting, normalized Top-k objective, softmax parameterization and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 4.1 expands the explanation of asymmetric weighting; the new Bottom-k objective is an experimental alternative, not a replacement for the proposed loss.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds OpenWebText as an attribution and evaluation corpus, extending the existing language-modeling coverage beyond WikiText-103. All original classification, diffusion and fine-grained attribution datasets remain. OpenWebText's membership in Llama3's pretraining data is explicitly assumed.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds the Rep. Dist. baseline attributed to Singla et al. (2023), ranking images by distance in MoCo ResNet-50 features. The comparator sets and gradient-method definitions in the retained experiments otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include pretrained Llama3-8B-Instruct evaluation using 500 generated queries and top-1 tail-patch updates, and group-scaled Gaussian perturbations during weight learning followed by clean-query evaluation. The ImageNet main-text revision from 500 to 1,000 queries matches v2's appendix rather than establishing an experimental increase. v3's diffusion counts remain inconsistent between Table 7 and Appendices B.2.1/B.4.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained k-sensitivity, loss and transfer analyses, v3 adds noise-robustness tests on ImageNet and ArtBench-2 (C.3/Figure 7), a Bottom-k-only loss ablation (C.4/Table 10), and language-attribution case studies for GPT-2-small and Llama3-8B-Instruct (C.7/Figures 8–11). These substantially extend scrutiny of the supervisory signal and retrieval behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 95% confidence intervals for LDS and tail-patch results. Added numerical comparisons use the existing reporting convention; no new repeated-run counts, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Matched existing result entries are retained, while v3 adds representation-distance scores, Bottom-k results, noise-response curves and language-retrieval examples. In the new OpenWebText experiment, Table 13 reports unweighted/weighted tail-patch scores of 0.04/0.65 for TracIn and 1.78/1.92 for LoGRA. Figure 7 additionally shows that sufficiently strong noise can erase or reverse weighting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 newly defines the normalized Bottom-k-only objective mathematically. The signal-plus-noise assumptions, optimal-weight derivation and SNR argument in Appendix A remain unchanged; the added metric-hacking remark supplies interpretation rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about parameter heterogeneity, self-supervised weight learning, improved attribution across domains and semantic specialization. The conclusion preserves these contributions; the additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly acknowledges residual off-target semantic influence, and the conclusion adds inherited biases from base attribution methods and constructed queries as a limitation. Appendix A argues against LDS metric hacking, while C.3/C.4 interpret noise robustness and weak negative-tail supervision. The original SNR interpretation and granularity limitation remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the new representation-distance baseline's feature extractor and distance, identifies the EKFAC implementation's codebase, and documents OpenWebText preprocessing into 99,642 sequences of 512 tokens and construction of 500 queries. Most existing implementation and optimization details are retained; the new data-summary table does not resolve conflicting diffusion query counts.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the representation-distance baseline, MoCo, OpenWebText and Llama3: Singla et al., He et al., Gokaslan et al. and Grattafiori et al. These support the added experiments; Section 2 and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify query-side weighting and data roles and expand the conclusion's limitations. Appendix C gains new subsections, with existing analyses renumbered. The abstract, introduction and overall narrative organization are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 adds the noise plot, four figures displaying language-retrieval comparisons, a data-usage table and a larger-model results table. It also expands Table 6 with a comparator row and the loss-ablation table with a Bottom-k column, and relocates appendix displays. Original Figures 1–6 are retained.

improvement.justification: The new noise tests and Bottom-k control strengthen empirical scrutiny of weight learning, while the added comparator, larger-model experiment and explicit bias limitations improve validation and transparency. The gain is limited: Table 7's diffusion counts conflict with B.2.1/B.4, and C.6 assumes OpenWebText was pretraining data, restricting the attribution interpretation of the new Llama results.
